topic: Poaceae in Testudo and Mediterranean tortoise diets

conclusion.supported: Wild Testudo graeca ibera are documented consuming Poaceae. Poaceae therefore must not be categorically marked unsuitable or indigestible for T. g. ibera solely because they are grasses.
conclusion.not_supported: The reviewed evidence does not support the blanket claim that Mediterranean Testudo cannot digest Poaceae, nor does wild occurrence establish that any grass species is an unlimited captive staple.
conclusion.implementation_rule: Assess grass taxa individually. Separate direct Ibera occurrence, plant identity/part and growth stage, captive digestive physiology, and husbandry guidance. Do not transfer grass-heavy diet rules from non-Testudo grazing tortoises to T. g. ibera without Testudo-specific evidence.

supports: More than 95% of observed diet was plant matter and 25 plant species were consumed.

Poaceae were part of the directly observed wild diet; the later eastern T. graeca synthesis reports Dactylis, Dichanthium, Festuca and Poa from this study and lists Poaceae among frequently consumed young plant material.
does_not_support: A universal captive percentage for grasses.
Unlimited feeding of every Poaceae species.
A claim that all grass life stages have equal digestibility or nutritional value.

sources.taxon: Testudo graeca eastern subspecies clades including T. g. ibera
supports: Poaceae are included among natural food families for eastern T. graeca.
The account summarizes the long-term Dobrogea Ibera observations and reports Poaceae among frequently consumed young vegetation.
Some eastern populations may shift toward Poaceae/cereals as summer vegetation dries, showing strong seasonal context.
does_not_support: Treating every eastern T. graeca population as ecologically identical.
Equating seasonal occurrence with optimal captive staple status.

supports: Tortoise food intake, digesta retention, digestibility and gut capacity can be studied quantitatively and differ with body size and taxon.
Digestive-physiology claims should be kept separate from plant-occurrence claims.
does_not_support: A plant-specific safety verdict for Poaceae.
The claim that T. g. ibera cannot digest grasses.

supports: A survey associated a summer diet category described as more than 80% grasses and weeds with husbandry outcomes.
does_not_support: Separating the effect of Poaceae from weeds because the survey grouped grasses and weeds together.

sources.author: Chris Leone
supports: Experienced Testudo husbandry context emphasizing low-protein, high-fiber, calcium-rich feeding and dietary diversity.
does_not_support: Replacing primary field or controlled scientific evidence.
Assigning a scientific evidence grade by itself.

guardrails: Do not label Poaceae as indigestible for Mediterranean Testudo without direct digestive evidence supporting that claim.
Do not infer captive feeding frequency from wild occurrence alone.
Do not generalize from desert/giant grazing tortoises to Testudo graeca ibera without an explicit applicability step.
Do not treat the combined survey category 'grasses and weeds' as Poaceae-specific evidence.
Plant species, part, maturity, fresh/dry state, season and population should be retained whenever the source reports them.
